note: RAISED 63670 -> 64026 (+356, all in `schema`) for D198: `create_routine` gained `revises`, the flag that REVISES an existing routine's recipe instead of creating one (the operator's answer, 2026-10-19: "Add a revise path to `create_routine` (or a sibling action) gated by a per-routine dial, like `config_confirm`"). The cost is one field description, and it is the only place a run learns the three things it cannot use the path safely without: that `prompt` carries the revision (one line per change, because the TARGET's run makes the edit from those words), that the target routine's own `revise_confirm` dial decides between a decision card and an immediate hand-over, and that the edit is made by that routine's next run and never by the caller — a run that believed it was writing another routine's files would propose a diff instead of prose, and a run not told the dial exists would re-issue a proposal that is already queued. Kept to a single clause: the dial's ladder, the proposer's capability and the refusal wording all live in the OBSERVATION the handler returns (engine/reviseroutine.py), which only a run that actually calls it pays for. No harness bullet was added — `create_routine`'s own bullet already names the kind, and a second always-on sentence about a mode most runs never use is what this budget exists to refuse. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: CUT 63712 -> 63670 (-42: harness -51, schema +9) by the Steward hub's retirement (operator, 2026-10-28): the finish summary now comes in two labelled parts, `**Process:**` (how the run went) then `**Work:**` (the task, its conditions and consequences), and the finish bullet names where decisions go instead of a page (a blocking ask when met, the rest batched before the finish). Paid for by the finish bullet no longer restating the schema's field list and by dropping the Markdown-rendering gloss (pipe tables, quotes) from both. PREVIOUS: CUT 63727 -> 63712 (-15, all in `schema`) by F787: the `questions` item schema's two decide-only sub-fields now lead with `decide ONLY:` so an ask_user batch is not offered a field askfields._DECIDE_ONLY refuses (folder-reorg:20261027-170451 turn 48 lost a turn to it), and the parent description stopped enumerating the per-question sub-fields the item schema already declares. The clarification is net-free: it pays for itself twice over. PREVIOUS: RAISED 62345 -> 63727 (+1382: +1008 `schema`, +374 `harness`) for D212 increment (a): one `ask_user` action may ask SEVERAL questions, and every filed decision record carries its CLASS. The cost is three things a run cannot use the feature without: the `questions` field's ask_user clause (the batch exists to be asked for), the new `blocks_work` field (the class override, whose description has to state the test it claims — `without this answer the run cannot do the work it was fired to do` — AND that it is not `mode`, because confusing the recorded class with the waiting mode is the one misreading that would make a run park itself), and the harness bullet that tells a run the batch exists at all. The first draft cost +2667; it was cut to this by dropping the justification prose from the bullet, shortening both clauses, and leaving the per-question sub-fields declared but undescribed (they mean for their question exactly what the same-named top-level field means, the way decide's items are already undescribed). What it buys back is measured, on the asking side rather than the contract: 37% of runs (60 of 163 over 282 real question records) already asked more than one question, up to 6, one action and one turn each, at a median 430 tokens of question prose per ask — so a run that batches 3 asks saves 2 turns of its own context, which is larger than 1382 chars, and the operator gets one grouped card set instead of 3 unrelated ones (51% of his answering sittings already disposed of several at once).
